newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 9.5/10.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 9.5/10.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 9.5/10.0 percent on Monday morning, dealers said.
They said liquidity was sufficient following early central bank injection of some 934 billion rupiah into the market.
One dealer said the rate did not fall although the central bank only offered papers (SBIs) longer than one-week.
"The market seems to be relatively stable. The central bank has stabilised the excess supply with longer-term papers," the dealer said, adding that longer-term rates were stable too.
One-month money was at 13.75/14.00 percent and three-month money was at 15.00/15.125 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 12.53 percent, compared with 9.92 percent on Thursday.
